narrative: Demand for PL1__MD9C45C2 is erratic (CV=0.549) with no detectable trend over the 131-day observation window from March 2025 to March 2026. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.49, range 0.28–5.74 days), making combined demand-lead-time uncertainty the primary safety stock driver. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: it responds immediately when stock hits the reorder point and orders a fixed EOQ lot, balancing the high ordering cost against holding cost at this low unit value. The current SAP policy orders at MOQ creating ~643 orders/year; the EOQ policy reduces this to ~21 orders/year, saving over 92% in total annual inventory cost while properly protecting the 95% service level.
warnings: Unstable lead time (CV=0.49): lead time variability is the dominant safety stock driver; supplier performance improvement would reduce required buffer.
Recommended safety stock (4,079) is 3.4x the current SAP safety stock (1,200); SAP baseline is insufficient for 95% SL given observed variability.
Peak inventory after replenishment (4,079 + 20,332 = 24,411 units) is within max_storage_units (24,741) with a margin of only 329 units — monitor for demand spikes.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material exhibits erratic but continuous demand (CV=0.549, non-zero fraction 96.9%) without trend or seasonality, making a continuous-review policy preferable to periodic review. The (r,Q) model is analytically tractable, directly incorporates combined demand and lead-time variance into the safety stock formula, and is well-suited for low-unit-cost, high-volume materials where ordering cost minimisation via EOQ is the dominant lever.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Peak stock (safety_stock + order_quantity = 24,411 units) leaves only 329 units of headroom against the 24,740 storage cap. Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g., due to worsening lead time variability) would breach capacity. A capacity-driven order-quantity reduction would increase ordering frequency and raise annual ordering costs.
